report_title: samen OSS Scan: Backlog Adoption Report
reader: Product leader selecting samen backlog items (Elixir/Ash SaaS foundry)
design_notes: Every one of the 127 findings files is assigned to exactly one section's `files` array.
The Executive Summary owns the 10 relevance:high files outright (their full deep-dive treatment lives there, not duplicated elsewhere).

Thematic deep-dive sections are built entirely from the 50 relevance:medium files, clustered into 7 real themes derived from the actual category/verdict data (not the high-relevance items, which are already fully covered in the Executive Summary).

Quick Hits is the single required medium-relevance catch-all for medium items too scattered across small categories (Developer Tools, Content Mgmt, Education, Games) to justify their own theme section.
Evaluated & Skipped closes the report with all 65 low + 2 none items (67 total), one line each.
Section order runs from most strategically central to samen's own architecture (agent-loop core patterns) outward to peripheral vertical-app patterns, ending in the scoreboard's long tail.

sections.title: Executive Summary & Scoreboard
sections.purpose: Fast top-of-report scoreboard: what to actually act on. Lists the 10 strongest adoption candidates (all relevance:high), each with project name, license, one-line verdict, and the specific samen gap/ADR it maps to. Includes a small counts table (10 high / 50 medium / 65 low / 2 none across 127 scanned repos) so the reader has denominator context before diving in.

file_notes.041-langchain-for-elixir.md: Do not depend on it (INV-4 risk), but mine trajectory-eval testing, tool-arg error feedback, GenAI OTel semconv, MessageDelta streaming for the AI plane.
file_notes.047-sagents.md: Do not adopt (LangChain dep, no masking chokepoint), but its LiveView streaming event taxonomy and HITL decision model map directly onto ADR-047.
file_notes.049-plausible-analytics.md: AGPL — patterns only. Cookie-less identity + ClickHouse ingestion + streamed export map onto samen's analytics/DSAR/status-page gaps.
file_notes.050-lightning.md: LGPL — patterns only. Production workflow-automation platform on samen's exact stack; run/snapshot execution model and retention discipline worth mining.
file_notes.070-keila.md: AGPL — patterns only. Delivery pipeline, per-sender rate limiting, bounce handling, MJML+Liquid templating for marketing/delivery scope.
file_notes.098-aethers3.md: Fills the open Storage.S3 skeleton gap directly; AP/CP split and honest-gaps doc style echo samen's own philosophy.
file_notes.100-boruta-server.md: OpenID-certified OAuth2/OIDC authorization-server umbrella — strongest reference (possible vendor candidate) for samen's deferred 'become an OIDC provider' gap.
file_notes.103-health.md: AGPL — patterns only. Targets the open G11 status-page gap; pull-mode active probing samen's push-only heartbeat lacks.
file_notes.108-osmotic.md: BSD-2-Clause (direct code study viable) but pre-adoption-stage (0 stars). Billing-ledger and fail-open/closed discipline map ~1:1 onto the G13 usage-rating gap.
file_notes.021-loomkin.md: Do not adopt its Jido/req_llm stack (already rejected), but steal the decision graph, keeper-based context offload, and mission-control UI ideas.

sections.title: Deep Dive: Agent Frameworks & Orchestration Libraries
sections.purpose: Elixir/OTP-native agent-loop and tool-orchestration libraries (the 'Agent Frameworks and Development Tools' category, medium tier). Directly informs samen's own ADR-047 agent-loop design: what governance, tool-calling, and multi-agent-coordination patterns other BEAM builders have already worked out.

sections.title: Deep Dive: Software Factories & Multi-Agent Dev Platforms
sections.purpose: Full 'AI-writes-software' orchestration platforms (build/plan/review/ship loops for coding agents) — the category samen's own autonomous-loop tooling most directly competes with and can learn UX/process patterns from. Includes one license-encumbered entrant (Svärm) called out inline rather than siloed, since it's substantively a software-factory play.

sections.title: Deep Dive: Agent Platforms With License Risk
sections.purpose: Agent/orchestration platforms that are technically relevant but carry licensing terms (source-available, non-OSS, field-of-use restrictions, etc.) that block direct adoption into MIT-licensed samen. Kept as its own section because the go/no-go call here is legal, not technical — a product leader needs this flagged distinctly rather than buried in a general agent-frameworks list.

sections.title: Deep Dive: AI Agent Products & Personal Assistants
sections.purpose: Single-user / personal-scale AI agent products (personal assistants, dreaming/memory agents, coding companions) built on Elixir/OTP. Wrong problem domain for samen's multi-tenant SaaS posture, but a dense source of pattern-mining ideas for the AI plane: memory, skills, self-scheduling, introspectable tool surfaces.

sections.title: Deep Dive: Data Pipelines, Realtime & Observability/Ops
sections.purpose: Plumbing samen needs regardless of vertical: change-data-capture/streaming (Sequin, Supabase Realtime), and operational visibility (Logflare log ingestion, Plural Console platform ops, ServiceRadar monitoring). Complements the high-relevance Health and AetherS3 findings already covered in the Executive Summary.

sections.title: Deep Dive: Business & Collaboration / Productivity SaaS
sections.purpose: Vertical Elixir/Phoenix SaaS products (scheduling, project/goal tracking, contract docs, team collaboration) whose domain models and multi-tenant UX patterns are directly analogous to what samen tenants will eventually build or what samen's own product surface could look like.

sections.title: Deep Dive: Communication & Social / Federation
sections.purpose: Fediverse/ActivityPub and social-communication platforms (Bonfire, Mobilizon, vutuv, etc.). Lower direct-adoption likelihood for a SaaS foundry, but real patterns around federation protocols, moderation, and social-graph data modeling worth a scoped look.

sections.title: Quick Hits (Medium Relevance, Miscellaneous)
sections.purpose: Remaining medium-relevance findings that don't cluster into a theme large enough to warrant its own deep-dive section — one project each from Developer Tools, Content Management, Education, and Games categories. One paragraph each: what it is, the one pattern worth noting, why it didn't rate a full section.

sections.title: Evaluated & Skipped
sections.purpose: Full accounting of every project scanned but not carried forward: all 65 relevance:low and 2 relevance:none findings, one line each (project name + one-line verdict), grouped by category for scanability. Exists so the reader can confirm nothing was silently dropped and spot-check any 'low' call they disagree with.
